supporting_observations.claim: At 13:42:41 UTC, dev.sharma added hana.ito to Billing-Share on DC-RB-01. This is the group addition matching the alert.
The group change's SubjectLogonId, 0x1307103b, matches dev.sharma's Kerberos network logon to DC-RB-01 from 10.60.10.23. Other endpoint telemetry identifies that address as WS-DSHARMA-01.

The observed actor, originating workstation, recipient, and destination group match the supplied administrative practices and scheduled afternoon Billing-Share onboarding change. This supports a benign disposition for the alerted activity.

The subsequent RDP logon to DC-RB-01 came from WS-DSHARMA-01 as dev.sharma, but occurred after the group addition and used a different logon ID, 0x13076620. It should not be treated as the session that performed the alerted change.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records establish the group-change identity and associated network logon, but do not show the command or administrative interface that submitted the change (S28-00016, S28-00018).
The change calendar supplies expected business context, but no underlying approval ticket accompanies the group-change record (S28-00018).
claims_not_established: The evidence does not independently establish who physically controlled dev.sharma's session when the change occurred (S28-00016, S28-00018).
The alerted event does not establish Remote Desktop Users membership or any other privileged-group addition; its recorded destination is Billing-Share (S28-00018).
unrelated_findings: Separate review: hana.ito's UserAssist registry entries reference powershell.exe at 13:49:41 and mstsc.exe at 14:11:25 on WS-HITO-01. These records do not provide commands, destinations, or proof of successful remote administration and do not establish maliciousness of the earlier Billing-Share change (S28-00043, S28-00054).

Separate software-policy review: dev.sharma launched Firefox with https://zoom.us/ and ran Zscaler's ZSATray.exe, neither listed among the supplied approved services/software. The Zscaler DLL signature was valid; these observations do not establish compromise or a connection to the group addition (S28-00009, S28-00030, S28-00032).

Separate session-timeline review: an mstsc.exe launch and successful FILE-RB-01 RDP logon occurred between the recorded workstation lock and unlock. The supplied records do not explain that sequence or connect it to the earlier group change (S28-00033, S28-00034, S28-00038, S28-00050).
